taxonomic_note: Accepted species; accepted varieties remain background taxonomy while the learner stays species-level.
look_here_first: Start with habit and leaflet size: a xeric shrub or small tree with tiny leathery, often nearly evergreen leaflets—commonly only three per leaf.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Bandera is the qualifying target-zone county retained by the latest review. Val Verde is documented but outside the project target list. Uvalde remains a lead, not locked evidence.

approval_exception.reason: Learner inclusion is independent from native-range certification.

best_field_traits: rocky limestone slopes and dry washes
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Much smaller and more xeric than Texas or Mexican ash; tiny coriaceous leaflets are the fastest field cue.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Tiny leathery compound leaflets plus xeric shrub habit; Fraxinus has samaras rather than drupes.

photo_note: Exact diagnostic imagery remains later enrichment. Manual library-first complementary photo selection installed; independent diagnostic ID review pending.

field_diagnostics.single_best_trait: Tiny thick leathery compound leaflets on a xeric shrub/small tree — a very different gestalt from the larger riparian/woodland ashes.
fastest_traits: Shrub or small tree rather than a large bottomland ash
Leaflets very small, thick/coriaceous and often glossy
Rocky limestone slopes, canyons and dry washes
Fraxinus confirmation from winged samaras rather than Forestiera-type drupes

look_alikes.distinction: Texas ash is a larger deciduous tree with larger 5–7 leaflets and a glaucous white-reticulate underside.
Mexican ash is a larger riparian/bottomland tree with 3–5(–7) larger sharply serrate leaflets and distinctive larger samaras.
Forestiera has simple leaves and fleshy drupes; Fraxinus has pinnately compound leaves and samaras.

unreliable_alone: three leaflets without confirming compound-leaf architecture
small stature on a young tree

diagnostic_photo_targets: Whole xeric shrub/small-tree habit in rocky habitat
Whole compound leaf with ruler showing 3–7 tiny leaflets
Close leaflet surface/texture showing coriaceous quality
